public_rationale: March 2022 experiments found that reducing misleading dataset correlations improved generalization for BERT, RoBERTa and ALBERT, supporting continued shortcut dependence during the period before September 23, 2022 [e6]. An April 2022 example found that sentiment-fine-tuned RoBERTa-large assigned an ambiguous sentence a positive label with 99.99% confidence; attribution methods highlighted sentiment-associated words [e7]. The March study also found better generalization from larger models and debiasing, so persistent shortcut dependence coexisted with genuine improvements [e6].
limitations: The evidence covers selected NLP models and tasks, not every leading model available by September 23, 2022 [e6, e7].
The single RoBERTa example does not establish prevalence [e7].
These studies do not establish a total absence of meaningful learning or directly measure the full breadth of human semantic flexibility [e6, e7].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: State-of-the-art models still learn to exploit spurious statistical patterns rather than learning meaning flexibly as humans do, so benchmark gains warrant caution.

statement.excerpt: But the smart money is still on being cautious about this, and in recognizing that what the Facebook researchers said in 2019 is still the case.

our_interpretation: The checkable assertion is that reliance on misleading statistical cues remained a problem for high-performing NLP systems in 2022. The advice to be cautious is not separately scored.
The plain reading concerns incomplete, unreliable generalization despite benchmark success. It does not require models to have learned no meaningful linguistic information whatsoever.

The ongoing state has no named reporting period. I use research reported during 2022 through September 23, the current research year up to publication; this field has no standard quarterly reporting cycle.
'State-of-the-art' is read as strong task-performing NLP models discussed in contemporary research, rather than every model or only the largest model released immediately before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary research finds that strong NLP models still rely on task-irrelevant cues or improve on controlled generalization tests when those cues are reduced, despite doing well on established tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary controlled studies establish that the relevant strong models have overcome the alleged shortcut dependence and reliably track task meaning when incidental statistical cues change.

evidence.explanation: Reducing misleading correlations improved independent-test performance for BERT and stronger RoBERTa and ALBERT models, supporting continued susceptibility in 2022. The same experiments found better generalization from larger models and debiasing, which limits any claim that no genuine progress occurred.

This illustrates persistent cue dependence, although the authors explicitly say the example does not establish prevalence.
